clue.text: Light to write — Desmond has restriction on reporting

indicators.note: reporting is speaking, so the words before are to be said out loud and heard as something else

parts.note: Des is the usual short form of the name Desmond; a clamp is something that restricts or holds fast, as in a clampdown

explanation.surface: A journalist called Desmond finds a reporting restriction stops him writing his story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reporting' signals the homophone: DES plus CLAMP, said out loud, sounds like the answer. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp standing on a desk gives light for writing by.

clue.text: Swallow the wrong way and do it again — something may be snatched from its jaws

definitions.text: something may be snatched from its jaws

indicators.note: the wrong way means backwards, so the word just before reads from its end

parts.note: fed means swallowed food, as in the cows fed
to swallow again is simply to eat

explanation.surface: Someone chokes on food and tries once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses the swallowing word; to 'do it again' is to swallow once more. The definition leans on the saying about snatching victory from the jaws of loss.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is snatching victory from the jaws of a loss, so a loss is what has jaws.

clue.text: Despicable person to apply insecticide?

definitions.meaning: to spray a jet of liquid, as with a bug spray

explanation.definitionFit: A squirt is a contemptible upstart, and to squirt is to spray a jet of liquid such as bug killer.

clue.text: Student at Aberdeen perhaps, showing off about wine e-three given here

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plates of a learner driver
Aberdeen stands on the River Don, so a place there is on Don

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: airs, as in putting on airs, is showing off
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A Scottish student boasts about the port wine on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. Aberdeen, a Scottish city, stands on the River Don; 'perhaps' marks it as one example. The theme's three airports are Heathrow, Luton and Stansted.
explanation.definitionFit: The three themed entries, Heathrow, Luton and Stansted, are all airfields serving the capital.

clue.text: Poor Beth, taken in by the wife, to be left at the station?

definitions.text: to be left at the station

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: missus is informal for a wife

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters of the word after are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unlucky Beth, fooled by a spouse, is stranded on the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' signals the anagram and 'taken in by' the container; the definition is the literal sense of the idiom for losing a chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing transport means being stranded, and the idiom also means losing an opportunity.

clue.text: Ancient philosopher and prince during setback

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside another
back says the word just before it runs the other way

parts.note: taken as written, the first half of the word setback
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: An old thinker and a royal suffer a reverse together.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'setback' does double duty in the surface: it splits as 'set' plus the reversal signal 'back', while 'during' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Thales of Miletus was the first Greek philosopher, of the sixth century BC.

clue.text: He has a shot at one of the three

parts.note: a throw is a shot or attempt, as in a throw at the coconut shy

explanation.surface: A man tries his luck at one of three targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'at' are link words. The three are the theme's London airports.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is the largest of the airports serving the capital.

clue.text: One of the three who is heard at Adam's mansion

parts.note: Luton is one of the theme's three London airports

indicators.note: is heard says the word before is spoken out loud and written as it sounds

parts.note: taken as written, to be heard

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is audible at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is heard' turns WHO into HOO. Luton Hoo is a country house in Bedfordshire designed by the architect Robert Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton Hoo, a Bedfordshire stately home, was built to Robert Adam's design.

clue.text: One of the three from pole to pole inside had a flavour

parts.note: S is the south pole

indicators.note: inside means within, so the second pole goes into the next piece

parts.note: tasted means had a flavour, as in it tasted of salt
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: An explorer, crossing from one end of the earth to the other, savours the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from pole to pole' gives one pole (S) at the start and the other (N) set 'inside' TASTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stansted is an Essex airport serving the capital, one of the theme's three.

clue.text: Another possible site than the three given here was…(obscenity)

definitions.text: Another possible site than the three given here
definitions.meaning: an island off the Essex coast once proposed for a new London airport

explanation.walkthrough: Foulness is an island in Essex, east of London, considered as a third London airport site in the 1970s alongside the theme's three airports.
explanation.definitionFit: Foulness Island was the planned Maplin airport site of the 1970s, and the word also means filthiness or obscene vileness.

clue.text: Chap with skill backed holy word

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: backed means turned around, so the word before is read from its end

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A man with a talent for religion chants a sacred phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' is the reversal signal; 'with' is a link word. The newspaper text read 'skilled', a misprint for 'skill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred syllable or phrase repeated in Hindu and Buddhist meditation.

clue.text: See 3
Objects to disturbed nights

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about broken sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a verb (complains) but is the plural noun; 'disturbed' rearranges NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Things are objects, items of any kind.

clue.text: South American capital, say, raised or get it for yourself?

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is lifted up, read from the bottom

parts.note: e.g. means for example, just as say does
get own, as in go and get your own

explanation.surface: Someone told to fetch something themselves is pointed to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EG into GE; OR is as written; 'get it for yourself' is the phrase GET OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgetown is the capital city of Guyana.

clue.text: Unorthodox part of stuff deposited so far

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, the tail end being cut away

parts.note: a heretic is someone of unorthodox belief, used here as a noun-adjective
ore is mineral matter laid down in deposits

explanation.surface: Unconventional sediment is said to have been dumped until now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' keeps only HERET of HERETIC (unorthodox); OF is as written and ORE is the deposited stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretofore is a formal word meaning up to this time, hitherto.

clue.text: Pursuit taking in fashionable article in distant waters

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit
in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A hunt for a stylish item leads to far-off seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' signals the container. 'distant waters' is fair to a British solver: the China Sea is on the far side of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The China Sea, East and South, lies off East Asia, far from Britain.

clue.text: Reductions (in manpower) overhead?

definitions.meaning: cutbacks in the staff of a ship or aircraft
very short haircuts, which sit on top of the head

explanation.definitionFit: Cuts to a ship's staff are reductions in personnel, and a close-cropped hairstyle sits on top of the head.

clue.text: See 21
Urges reform in store, one of those paraded in the capital

definitions.text: one of those paraded in the capital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a hoard is a stored stock

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushes for change in a shop, with a ceremonial parade in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' signals the anagram and 'in' the container. The Horse Guards are cavalry who parade in London, for example at Trooping the Colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Horse Guard is a soldier of the Household Cavalry, seen on ceremonial parade in London.

clue.text: Undeveloped part of root system bryophytes don't need

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Mosses get by without a proper root system.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'systEM BRYOphytes'. Bryophytes are mosses and liverworts, which have no true roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in embryo is at its earliest stage, not yet grown.

clue.text: Direction about drink with jet?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: ENE is east-north-east, a compass direction
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone gives directions for a drink alongside a jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'with' is a link word, and the definition leans on the phrase jet engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet is a type of motor that drives an aircraft, so the word is an example of the general kind.

clue.text: Escape with musical instrument in black box

parts.note: flight is escape, as in taking flight
the recorder is a wind instrument

explanation.surface: Someone gets away carrying an instrument hidden in a dark case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'in' are link words. The black box on an aircraft records flight data.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's black box is the device that logs cockpit data for crash investigators.

clue.text: The force of recent fashion?

parts.note: recent means new
ton is an old word for fashion, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: Asks what drives modern trends.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for fashion is an old borrowing from French. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The newton is the SI unit of force, named after Isaac Newton.

clue.text: End of journey for duck, about the right time?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
min is short for minute, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A duck's journey ends at about the correct hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'for' and 'the' are link words. 'duck' looks like the subject of the journey but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the building or station where a route finishes, such as an airport terminal.

clue.text: Learned work about river that should stand up to criticism?

definitions.text: that should stand up to criticism

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: a study is a scholarly piece of work
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: An academic paper on a river ought to withstand critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts STUDY around R, making STU-R-DY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sturdy is robust, strong enough to withstand attack.

clue.text: Beginning journey to school or house

definitions.meaning: getting on a plane or ship at the start of a trip
the word that goes before school or house for a place where you live in

explanation.walkthrough: Boarding school and boarding house are both places of residence; boarding a plane fits the airport theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers start a flight by getting aboard, and a residential school or lodging house takes the same word in front.

clue.text: Say — say it can't lose!

indicators.note: say tells you to speak the next words out loud and hear them as another word

parts.note: a cert is a racing term for a certainty, a horse that cannot lose

explanation.surface: A gambler insists that the bet is a sure winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' (the second one) signals the homophone: 'a cert' spoken sounds like the answer. A cert is British slang for a certain winner.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state firmly, declare.

clue.text: Without respect en route for Isle of Wight?

definitions.text: en route for Isle of Wight?
definitions.meaning: the ferry crossing to the Isle of Wight is across the Solent strait

explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, so travellers there are 'in Solent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rude and disrespectful, and split in two it says you are on the strait to Wight.
